# Drawbridge

> Drawbridge is the sign-in gateway we're building for Citadel, Wayne State's container platform: Apache with mod_auth_openidc as one OpenID Connect client for Microsoft Entra ID. It drops any identity header a visitor sends and passes the app a 60-second ES256-signed assertion that SESAME checks. It isn't in front of any apps yet.

**Comes down for signed-in people.**

Checks: `composer ci` (the same command runs on GitLab and GitHub). The container rig has its own script, see "Run the checks".

> The one way into the Citadel. It only comes down for people who signed in.

Drawbridge is the sign-in gateway for the apps on Citadel, Wayne State's container platform. It is Apache with
mod_auth_openidc, set up as one OpenID Connect client for Microsoft Entra ID. It is not live yet: its home will be
`auth.apps.wayne.edu`, in front of every app on the platform, once the Citadel routing for it exists. Release 0.2 is
unreleased; so far only the gateway image is built, and it will run as a service on Citadel. As a reverse proxy it
checks that the visitor has a session, drops any identity header the visitor sent, and passes the app either a
short-lived signed assertion that SESAME's `gateway` driver verifies, or plain `X-Authenticated-*` headers for apps
that cannot verify a token yet. Which paths need a login, and which need an Entra authentication context on top, is
declared per app in a config file. Nothing else decides it.

Why a moat and not a lock on every door: each app doing its own OpenID Connect is another chance to get a nonce,
a state check or a token signature wrong. We'd rather get that right once, in a maintained module
(mod_auth_openidc). Each app then checks one small signed token.

Development happens on Wayne State's GitLab. This GitHub repository is a read-only release mirror: `main` and tags
are copied here automatically, and changes, issues and merge requests go to GitLab first.

Every page below is Markdown. The HTML pages send the same Markdown to a client that asks for `text/markdown`. Written by Squire's agent-ready kit from the README and the pages; do not edit.

## Pages

- [Drawbridge: Comes down for signed-in people](https://drawbridge.apps.wayne.edu/index.md): Drawbridge is the sign-in gateway we're building for Citadel, Wayne State's container platform: Apache with mod_auth_openidc as one OpenID Connect client for Microsoft Entra ID. It drops any identity header a visitor sends and passes the app a 60-second ES256-signed assertion that SESAME checks. It isn't in front of any apps yet.

## Prompts

- [Get started with Drawbridge](https://drawbridge.apps.wayne.edu/#prompt-get-started): Clone, validate the example config, ask explain about three doors, and run the rig against a mock provider. Nothing reaches Entra. The prompt itself is in https://drawbridge.apps.wayne.edu/index.md.
- [A Laravel app behind Drawbridge](https://drawbridge.apps.wayne.edu/#prompt-laravel): Its door schedule for the gate, and SESAME's gateway driver checking the signed assertion on the way in. The prompt itself is in https://drawbridge.apps.wayne.edu/index.md.
- [A raw PHP app behind Drawbridge](https://drawbridge.apps.wayne.edu/#prompt-raw-php): The same door schedule, and SESAME's gateway driver built by hand, with the check placed before any output. The prompt itself is in https://drawbridge.apps.wayne.edu/index.md.
